places.name: Gangaramaya Temple
places.overview: A busy Buddhist temple in central Colombo that mixes Sri Lankan, Thai and Chinese styles.
places.why: An easy first taste of temple life if you only have a day in the city.
places.access: Tuk tuk or taxi from Fort or Pettah, about 15 minutes.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off inside.

places.name: Galle Face Green
places.overview: A long seaside promenade in Colombo where families fly kites and food stalls open at sunset.
places.why: The best free evening in the capital.
places.access: Walk from Fort, or take a tuk tuk.

places.name: Negombo Beach
places.overview: A long sandy beach close to the international airport, with fishing boats and an easy pace.
places.why: A gentle first or last night, about 30 minutes from the airport.
places.access: Taxi from the airport.
places.verify: outside land by 0.1 km, nearest gampaha

places.name: Negombo Lagoon
places.overview: A wide lagoon of mangroves and small fishing boats just south of town.
places.why: A quiet boat ride with birds and fishermen at work.
places.access: Boat operators near the lagoon road.
places.verify: outside land by 1.3 km, nearest gampaha

places.name: Kalutara Bodhiya
places.overview: A large white hollow stupa beside the Kalu Ganga river, and a common stop on the coast road.
places.why: You can walk inside the stupa, which is unusual.
places.access: On the Galle Road in Kalutara.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off inside.

places.name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
places.overview: The most important Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka, beside Kandy Lake. It holds a relic of the Buddha.
places.why: Evening ceremonies with drums are the most atmospheric time to visit.
places.access: Walk from Kandy town and the lake.
places.dress: White clothing is respectful. Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off.

places.name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya
places.overview: Wide gardens beside the Mahaweli River, known for orchids, giant bamboo and old avenues of palms.
places.why: A calm half day with plenty of shade.
places.access: About 20 minutes by road from Kandy.

places.name: Sigiriya Rock
places.overview: A palace built on a rock about 200 metres above the forest in the fifth century, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.why: The climb passes frescoes, the mirror wall and the lion paws before a wide view at the top.
places.access: About 4 hours by road from the airport. Nearest town is Dambulla.
places.walk: Hard. About 1,200 steps with some exposed stairs.
places.dress: Good shoes, water and a hat. Go at opening time.

places.name: Dambulla Cave Temple
places.overview: Five caves filled with Buddha statues and painted ceilings, high on a granite rock. A destination in Matale District.
places.why: The painted caves are among the finest in the country.
places.access: In Dambulla town, on the main road north.
places.walk: Moderate. A steady walk up stone steps.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off at the caves.

places.name: Riverston
places.overview: A cool, misty ridge on the northern edge of the Knuckles range, far from the tour bus routes.
places.why: Short walks with big views, in a very different climate from Sigiriya in the same district.
places.access: A winding road from Matale town through Rattota.
places.dress: Bring a light jacket and leech socks in wet months.

places.name: Gregory Lake
places.overview: A small lake in the middle of Nuwara Eliya, the highest town on the island's tourist trail.
places.why: An easy stroll in cool air, close to old bungalows and tea factories.
places.access: Walk from Nuwara Eliya town.

places.name: Horton Plains and World's End
places.overview: A high plateau of grassland and cloud forest ending at a cliff with a long view south.
places.why: Clouds often roll in by 10 am, so an early start pays off.
places.access: About 1 hour by road from Nuwara Eliya. Leave before dawn.

places.name: Nine Arch Bridge
places.overview: A curved stone railway bridge set among tea and forest near Ella.
places.why: Check train times and watch one cross.
places.access: A short tuk tuk ride or a walk from Ella town.
places.dress: Good shoes. Stay clear of the rails.

places.name: Little Adam's Peak
places.overview: A short walk through tea to a rounded summit above the Ella Gap.
places.why: One of the best views for the least effort in the hills.
places.access: Starts on the edge of Ella town.
places.walk: Moderate. Some steps near the top.

places.name: Ella Rock
places.overview: A longer hike along the railway line and up through forest to a high ledge.
places.why: A real hike with a big reward. A guide helps on the unmarked paths.
places.access: Starts near Ella station or Kithalella.
places.dress: Good shoes, water, an early start.

places.name: Diyaluma Falls
places.overview: One of the tallest waterfalls in Sri Lanka, with natural pools above the drop.
places.why: The upper pools are a beautiful place to rest. Take care near the edge.
places.access: On the road from Wellawaya to Haputale, near Koslanda.
places.walk: Moderate to hard to reach the upper pools.
places.dress: Good shoes. Swim only with local advice.

places.name: Kataragama Sacred City
places.overview: A holy town shared by Buddhist, Hindu and Muslim pilgrims.
places.why: The evening puja brings drums, fire and crowds of families.
places.access: About 30 minutes by road from Tissamaharama.

places.name: Yala National Park
places.overview: The best known park in the country, with a good chance of leopards, elephants and sloth bears.
places.why: Dawn drives give the best sightings. No animal is ever promised.
places.access: Jeeps leave from Tissamaharama and Kirinda for the Palatupana gate.
places.walk: None. You stay in the jeep.

places.name: Tangalle Beach
places.overview: Long empty beaches and quiet bays on the far south coast.
places.why: Slower and less built up than the beaches further west.
places.access: On the coast road, about 1 hour from Mirissa.

places.name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
places.overview: The country's best known rainforest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, rich in birds found nowhere else.
places.why: Walk with a local guide early in the morning.
places.access: Kudawa entrance, reached by road from Ratnapura.
places.walk: Moderate. Forest paths can be muddy.
places.dress: Long trousers and leech socks in wet months.

places.name: Udawalawe National Park
places.overview: Open grassland around a large reservoir, and the easiest place to see elephants in the wild.
places.why: Elephants are seen on almost every drive.
places.access: Jeeps leave from Udawalawe town near the park gate.
places.walk: None. You stay in the jeep.

places.name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
places.overview: A sacred mountain climbed by pilgrims of several faiths, usually overnight to reach the summit for sunrise.
places.why: The season usually runs from December to May, with lit paths and tea stalls.
places.access: Most walkers start from Dalhousie.
places.dress: Warm layers for the summit. Shoes off at the shrine.

places.name: Kitulgala
places.overview: A river town in the wet zone, known for white water rafting on the Kelani.
places.why: An active stop on the way between Colombo and the hills.
places.access: On the road between Colombo and Hatton.

places.name: Galle Fort
places.overview: A walled old town by the sea, first built by the Portuguese and expanded by the Dutch. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.why: Walk the ramparts at sunset, after the day visitors leave.
places.access: About 2 to 3 hours from the airport by expressway.

places.name: Unawatuna and Jungle Beach
places.overview: A sheltered curved bay close to Galle, with a smaller beach reached through trees.
places.why: Calm water in season, 15 minutes from the fort.
places.access: Tuk tuk from Galle.

places.name: Hikkaduwa
places.overview: A lively beach town with reef close to the shore and sea turtles often seen in the shallows.
places.why: An easy stop on the coast railway.
places.access: On the coast road and railway.

places.name: Mirissa Beach
places.overview: A palm lined bay and the main base for whale watching, mostly from November to April.
places.why: Whales in season, and slow beach days any time the sea is calm.
places.access: On the coast road, about 1 hour from Galle.
places.dress: Casual. Seas can be rough on boat trips.

places.name: Weligama Bay
places.overview: A wide bay with gentle waves, popular for first surf lessons.
places.why: One of the easiest places on the island to learn to surf.
places.access: On the coast road next to Mirissa.

places.name: Koneswaram Temple
places.overview: A Hindu temple on Swami Rock, high above the sea at Trincomalee.
places.why: Sea views and a lively shrine at the end of an old fort road.
places.access: Through Fort Frederick in Trincomalee.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off.

places.name: Nilaveli Beach
places.overview: A long pale beach north of Trincomalee, and the boat point for Pigeon Island.
places.why: Calm swimming when the south coast is rough, from about April to September.
places.access: About 30 minutes by road from Trincomalee.

places.name: Pasikudah Bay
places.overview: A shallow, sheltered bay on the east coast with very calm water in season.
places.why: One of the gentlest swimming spots for families.
places.access: By road from Polonnaruwa or Batticaloa.

places.name: Batticaloa Fort
places.overview: A small Dutch fort surrounded by lagoon in the middle of Batticaloa.
places.why: A quiet look at the east coast's colonial past.
places.access: In Batticaloa town.

places.name: Arugam Bay
places.overview: A relaxed surf town with its best waves from about May to September.
places.why: Good surf and a slow village feel in the east coast season.
places.access: By road through Monaragala and Pottuvil.
places.verify: outside land by 0.1 km, nearest ampara

places.name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
places.overview: The ruins of a medieval royal capital, with great stone Buddhas at Gal Vihara. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.why: Flat and easy to see by bicycle.
places.access: About 1 hour by road from Sigiriya.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Sun protection.

places.name: Minneriya National Park
places.overview: A park around an ancient reservoir, where large herds of elephants gather from about July to October.
places.why: A late afternoon drive is the usual way to see them.
places.access: Jeeps from Sigiriya, Habarana and the park gate.
places.walk: None. You stay in the jeep.

places.name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
places.overview: The first great capital of Sri Lanka, with huge stupas and the sacred Sri Maha Bodhi tree. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.why: The scale of the old city surprises most visitors.
places.access: By road or train from Colombo.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. White is respectful. Shoes off.

places.name: Mihintale
places.overview: A hilltop shrine where Buddhism is said to have been introduced to the island.
places.why: A long stone stairway with wide views at sunset.
places.access: About 30 minutes by road from Anuradhapura.
places.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Shoes off at the top.

places.name: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
places.overview: A short lived medieval capital on a granite rock, with a steep ornamental stairway.
places.why: Far fewer visitors than Sigiriya.
places.access: By road, north of Kurunegala.

places.name: Wilpattu National Park
places.overview: The largest national park in the country, with thick forest, natural lakes and leopards.
places.why: Quieter tracks than Yala.
places.access: Hunuwilagama gate, by road from Anuradhapura or Puttalam.
places.walk: None. You stay in the jeep.

places.name: Kalpitiya
places.overview: A long sandy peninsula known for kitesurfing and lagoon life.
places.why: Strong steady wind in season and a very local feel.
places.access: By road north from Negombo.

places.name: Mannar Fort
places.overview: A Portuguese and Dutch fort at the entrance to Mannar Island.
places.why: A rarely visited corner of the island, known for baobab trees and migrating birds.
places.access: By road across the causeway to Mannar Island.

places.name: Jaffna Fort
places.overview: A large star shaped Dutch fort beside the Jaffna lagoon.
places.why: A walk on the walls shows how different the far north feels.
places.access: In Jaffna town, reached by road, train or domestic flight.

places.name: Nallur Kandaswamy Temple
places.overview: The most important Hindu temple in the north, and the heart of Jaffna's Tamil culture.
places.why: Visit at puja time, then try Jaffna crab curry nearby.
places.access: A short tuk tuk ride from Jaffna town.
places.dress: Men remove shirts inside. Shoes off.
